intro.displayText: Every app remembers things, and it keeps them in a database. Your mission: do a roll call at the Grove Critter Club by asking its database your very first questions!
intro.speechText: Every app remembers things, and it keeps them in a database. Your mission is to do a roll call at the Grove Critter Club, by asking its database your very first questions!

recap.displayText: Roll call done, and every critter answered! Your new word is query: a question you ask a database, like SELECT name FROM critters.
recap.speechText: Roll call done, and every critter answered! Your new word is query, which means a question you ask a database.

intro.displayText: Nearly every app keeps its data in a database, and SQL is how developers ask it questions. You'll learn how tables, rows, columns and primary keys fit together, and write SELECT queries with calculated columns. Then you'll fix a price list and build a stock report for Pixel Pier, a game shop.
intro.speechText: Nearly every app keeps its data in a database, and sequel is how developers ask it questions. You'll learn how tables, rows, columns and primary keys fit together, and write select queries with calculated columns. Then you'll fix a price list and build a stock report for Pixel Pier, a game shop.

recap.displayText: You can read a table's design and pull exactly the columns you need, calculated ones included. The gotcha to remember: a missing comma in a SELECT list isn't an error. SQL reads the second name as an alias, so check your result's column names.
recap.speechText: You can read a table's design and pull exactly the columns you need, calculated ones included. The gotcha to remember is a missing comma in a select list. It isn't an error, because sequel reads the second name as an alias, so always check your result's column names.

intro.displayText: The Critter Club is planning a party, and each invitation goes to different critters. Your mission: use WHERE to find exactly the right ones!
intro.speechText: The Critter Club is planning a party, and each invitation goes to different critters. Your mission is to use where to find exactly the right ones!

recap.displayText: Party invitations sorted! Your new word is condition: a test, like age > 3, that each row passes or fails.
recap.speechText: Party invitations sorted! Your new word is condition, a test like age greater than 3 that each row passes or fails.

intro.displayText: Real apps almost never want every row: a shop page shows one platform, and a search box shows only matches. WHERE is how you filter, and it's home to two of SQL's sneakiest bugs. You'll fix a restock list and a sale shelf, then write a title search.
intro.speechText: Real apps almost never want every row. A shop page shows one platform, and a search box shows only matches. Where is how you filter, and it's home to two of sequel's sneakiest bugs. You'll fix a restock list and a sale shelf, then write a title search.

recap.displayText: You can filter with comparisons, AND, OR, IN, BETWEEN, LIKE and IS NULL. The gotcha to remember: = NULL and <> NULL never match anything, because a comparison with NULL is unknown. Use IS NULL and IS NOT NULL instead.
recap.speechText: You can filter with comparisons, and, or, in, between, like, and is null. The gotcha to remember is that equals null never matches anything, because a comparison with null is unknown. Use is null and is not null instead.

intro.displayText: The Critter Club is lining up for the Grove parade! Your mission: put the critters in order, by name and by age, and pick the 3 leaders for the front.
intro.speechText: The Critter Club is lining up for the Grove parade! Your mission is to put the critters in order, by name and by age, and pick the 3 leaders for the front.

recap.displayText: The parade is ready to march! Your new word is sort: putting rows in order, like A to Z or oldest first.
recap.speechText: The parade is ready to march! Your new word is sort, which means putting rows in order, like A to Z or oldest first.

intro.displayText: Every list in an app has an order: cheapest first, newest first, A to Z. You'll sort with ORDER BY, remove repeats with DISTINCT, and split long lists into pages with LIMIT and OFFSET. Then you'll fix Pixel Pier's price list and build its platform menu and catalog pages.
intro.speechText: Every list in an app has an order, like cheapest first, newest first, or A to Z. You'll sort with order by, remove repeats with distinct, and split long lists into pages with limit and offset. Then you'll fix Pixel Pier's price list and build its platform menu and catalog pages.

recap.displayText: You can sort on several columns, remove repeats and page through results. The gotcha to remember: without ORDER BY, SQL promises no order at all, and rows that tie keep no promise either. Sort whenever order matters, and add a tiebreaker for paging.
recap.speechText: You can sort on several columns, remove repeats, and page through results. The gotcha to remember is that without order by, sequel promises no order at all, and rows that tie keep no promise either. Sort whenever order matters, and add a tiebreaker for paging.
